Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: A comparative analysis of Inconel 718 made by additive manufacturing and suction casting: Microstructure evolution in homogenization

Composition_Info.Note: Ni was treated as balance to 100 wt.% from Table 1.

Process_Text.original: One rod shape sample of Inconel 718 with a diameter of 11 mm and a length of 40 mm was prepared by suction-casting under a pure argon atmosphere using an arc-melter (ABJ-338, manufactured by Materials Research Furnaces Inc).
Process_Text.simplified: Inconel 718 was prepared as a suction-cast rod under pure argon using an ABJ-338 arc-melter. Rod size was 11 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length.

Process_Info.Equipment: Arc-melter ABJ-338, Materials Research Furnaces Inc

Microstructure_Text.original: In the as-cast sample, the grains formed during the solidification are equiaxial with a diameter between 10 and 20 μm. Irregular-shaped Nb-rich Laves_C14 phase forms along grain boundaries as the predominant precipitate. A small fraction of blocky NbC carbides is encompassed by the Laves_C14 precipitates. The δ phase can be observed neither in the alloys by suction-casting nor LPBF.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: As-cast suction-cast Inconel 718 shows equiaxed grains of 10-20 μm. Laves_C14 is the predominant grain-boundary precipitate, with a small fraction of blocky NbC carbides. No δ phase was observed.

Composition_Info.Note: Ni was treated as balance to 100 wt.% from Table 1.

Process_Text.original: One rod shape sample of Inconel 718 with a diameter of 11 mm and a length of 40 mm was prepared by suction-casting under a pure argon atmosphere using an arc-melter (ABJ-338, manufactured by Materials Research Furnaces Inc). The alloy was sectioned into parts and encapsulated into vacuumed quartz tubes with back-filled pure argon. Afterward, the sample was homogenized at 1180 °C for 20 min followed by quenching in ice-water.
Process_Text.simplified: Suction-cast Inconel 718 was vacuum-encapsulated with argon backfill, homogenized at 1180 °C for 20 min, and then quenched in ice-water.

Process_Info.Equipment: Arc-melter ABJ-338, Materials Research Furnaces Inc

Microstructure_Text.original: For the suction-cast alloys, 20-min homogenization at 1180 °C can dissolve most of the Laves_C14 phase in the as-cast microstructure and remain the NbC carbides formed during solidification. However, some remaining Laves_C14 particles can still be observed near the NbC carbides. The unimodal grain size distribution indicates a uniform grain growth during the homogenization of the as-cast samples at 1180 °C for 20 min.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: After 20 min homogenization, most Laves_C14 dissolves while solidification-formed NbC remains. Some residual Laves_C14 is still present near NbC, and the grain-size distribution indicates uniform grain growth.

Composition_Info.Note: Ni was treated as balance to 100 wt.% from Table 1.

Microstructure_Text.original: For the suction-cast alloys, 1-h homogenization at 1180 °C can dissolve most of the Laves_C14 phase in the as-cast microstructure and remain the NbC carbides formed during solidification. Some remaining Laves_C14 particles can still be observed near the NbC carbides. A bimodal grain size distribution indicates a discontinuous grain growth. The left peak of the grain size distribution curve of AC1h implies the initial grains, and the right peak represents the grown grains from AC20m.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: After 1 h homogenization, most Laves_C14 has dissolved but residual Laves_C14 remains near NbC. Grain growth becomes discontinuous, with a bimodal grain-size distribution.

The alloy was sectioned into parts and encapsulated into vacuumed quartz tubes with back-filled pure argon. Afterward, the sample was homogenized at 1180 °C for 12 h followed by quenching in ice-water.
Process_Text.simplified: Suction-cast Inconel 718 was vacuum-encapsulated with argon backfill, homogenized at 1180 °C for 12 h, and then quenched in ice-water.

Process_Info.Equipment: Arc-melter ABJ-338, Materials Research Furnaces Inc

Microstructure_Text.original: After 12-h homogenization, the Laves_C14 phase dissolves completely, and only NbC carbides can be observed as precipitates. Significantly coarsened grains can be found in sample AC12h with some small grains remained at the triple junctions of these coarsened grains. A trimodal grain size distribution can also be observed, of which two peaks appear with smaller grain diameters of 150 μm and 400 μm. The distinct large and small grains indicate an abnormal grain growth during homogenization.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: After 12 h homogenization, Laves_C14 is fully dissolved and only NbC remains. The microstructure shows abnormal grain growth with very coarse grains, retained small grains at triple junctions, and trimodal grain-size characteristics.

Process_Text.original: AM Inconel 718 samples were built by LPBF using an EOS M 290 machine with default laser melting parameters with the laser power of 285 W, the scan velocity of 960 mm/s, and the hatching space of 0.11 mm. The hatch lines between adjacent layers have a rotation angle of 67°.
Process_Text.simplified: Inconel 718 was built by LPBF on an EOS M 290 using 285 W laser power, 960 mm/s scan velocity, 0.11 mm hatch spacing, and 67° layer-to-layer hatch rotation.

Microstructure_Text.original: The as-built microstructure of the X-Z plane shows that due to the large directional thermal gradient introduced by laser melting, columnar grains grow along the direction normal to the edge of single arc-shaped melt pools. Both very fine columnar subgrains with a width of about 1 μm and cellular subgrains with a diameter of about 2 μm can be found within the relatively larger grains of the overlapped melt pool areas. The only secondary phase observed in the as-built sample is the Laves_C14 phase, which forms along grain boundaries of both the columnar and cellular subgrains due to Nb segregation.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: The as-built LPBF alloy contains melt-pool-associated columnar grains and fine columnar/cellular subgrains. Laves_C14 is the only observed secondary phase and forms along subgrain boundaries because of Nb segregation.

Composition_Info.Note: Ni was treated as balance to 100 wt.% from Table 1.

Process_Text.original: AM Inconel 718 samples were built by LPBF using an EOS M 290 machine with default laser melting parameters with the laser power of 285 W, the scan velocity of 960 mm/s, and the hatching space of 0.11 mm. The hatch lines between adjacent layers have a rotation angle of 67°. The built alloy was sectioned into parts and encapsulated into vacuumed quartz tubes with back-filled pure argon. Afterward, the sample was homogenized at 1180 °C for 20 min followed by quenching in ice-water.
Process_Text.simplified: LPBF Inconel 718 built on an EOS M 290 was vacuum-encapsulated with argon backfill, homogenized at 1180 °C for 20 min, and then quenched in ice-water.

Microstructure_Text.original: For the AM alloys, 20-min homogenization causes the Laves_C14 phase formed in the as-built condition to dissolve into the γ matrix completely. Meanwhile, only a very small amount of NbC carbides can be found to form along grain boundaries in sample AM20m. The small peak at a grain diameter of 50 μm in the grain size distribution curve indicates the initiation of recrystallization in sample AM20m.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: After 20 min homogenization, Laves_C14 dissolves completely and only a very small amount of NbC appears at grain boundaries. Recrystallization has initiated, as indicated by a 50 μm grain-size peak.

Composition_Info.Note: Ni was treated as balance to 100 wt.% from Table 1.

Process_Text.original: AM Inconel 718 samples were built by LPBF using an EOS M 290 machine with default laser melting parameters with the laser power of 285 W, the scan velocity of 960 mm/s, and the hatching space of 0.11 mm. The hatch lines between adjacent layers have a rotation angle of 67°. The built alloy was sectioned into parts and encapsulated into vacuumed quartz tubes with back-filled pure argon. Afterward, the sample was homogenized at 1180 °C for 1 h followed by quenching in ice-water.
Process_Text.simplified: LPBF Inconel 718 built on an EOS M 290 was vacuum-encapsulated with argon backfill, homogenized at 1180 °C for 1 h, and then quenched in ice-water.

Microstructure_Text.original: Microstructure evolution during homogenization at 1180 °C for a long time can promote more NbC carbide formation. After 1-h homogenization, three distinct peaks can be observed in the grain size distribution curve for sample AM1h. The average grain size of sample AM1h becomes a smaller value of 128 μm. Sample AM1h shows the lowest and uniform GOS distribution, indicating almost all grains are continuously recrystallized.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: After 1 h homogenization, NbC formation increases, the grain-size distribution becomes multimodal, the average grain size decreases to 128 μm, and the alloy is almost fully continuously recrystallized.

Composition_Info.Note: Ni was treated as balance to 100 wt.% from Table 1.

Process_Text.original: AM Inconel 718 samples were built by LPBF using an EOS M 290 machine with default laser melting parameters with the laser power of 285 W, the scan velocity of 960 mm/s, and the hatching space of 0.11 mm. The hatch lines between adjacent layers have a rotation angle of 67°. The built alloy was sectioned into parts and encapsulated into vacuumed quartz tubes with back-filled pure argon. Afterward, the sample was homogenized at 1180 °C for 12 h followed by quenching in ice-water.
Process_Text.simplified: LPBF Inconel 718 built on an EOS M 290 was vacuum-encapsulated with argon backfill, homogenized at 1180 °C for 12 h, and then quenched in ice-water.

Microstructure_Text.original: Long-time homogenization at 1180 °C promotes more NbC carbide formation, and a notable increase of the particle size of NbC carbides can be identified in sample AM12h by comparison with samples AM20m and AM1h. After 12-h homogenization, the average grain size value in sample AM12h decreases further down to 113 μm. The grain size distribution of AM12h is close to unimodal. Dispersed NbC particles distribute along and near grain boundaries, indicating that the fine NbC carbides precipitating along with recrystallization at or near grain boundaries can impede grain boundary movement effectively and hence refine the grain size. Direct evidence of dislocation loops emitted from larger NbC carbides of about 200 nm in diameter was observed, and dislocation-precipitate interactions follow both Orowan bowing and dislocation cutting mechanisms.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: After 12 h homogenization, NbC fraction and particle size increase, the average grain size further decreases to 113 μm, and the grain-size distribution becomes nearly unimodal. Fine NbC near grain boundaries provides Zener pinning during continuous recrystallization. Larger NbC particles around 200 nm act as dislocation sources, and both cutting and bowing mechanisms are observed.
